_comment: Runtime component adoption register. Its sibling, provenance/upstreams.json, records mechanisms assimilated into this repository's own code under ADR-004. The split is deliberate and is the difference between installing something and becoming something: a DEPENDENCY is called at runtime and leaves a runtime trace; an assimilated mechanism runs as AETHRION's own code and leaves none. Every entry here transcribes a decision already recorded in docs/architecture/AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md, an ADR, or the package that owns the integration. A null obligation field is not an oversight - it is an unresolved acquisition decision, and scripts/check_wp_implementation_sources.py reports it as one.

adoption_types.DEPENDENCY: Called at runtime, not copied. Version pinning, failure semantics and an upgrade path are the obligation.
adoption_types.ADAPTER: An external component held behind an AETHRION contract. The obligation is that the contract survives replacing it.
adoption_types.OPTIONAL_BACKEND: A deployment choice behind a capability interface. The interface is the contract, not the backend, and the choice must be recorded rather than made implicitly.
adoption_types.STANDARD: A format or model implemented as specified. Conformance testing is the obligation.
adoption_types.PATTERN: An architectural idea implemented here with no code taken and nothing called. Attribution and honesty about divergence are the obligation.

statuses.PROPOSED: Decided on paper. Nothing is installed, and the obligations below are unresolved.
statuses.QUALIFIED: Version or image digest pinned, failure semantics written, and the obligations for its type resolved.
statuses.INTEGRATED: Running behind its AETHRION contract and accepted by an independent verifier.

entries.name: Temporal
entries.owned_contract: The G0–G10 gate lifecycle and its transition authority. Workflow definitions, the ProjectLifecycle skeleton and every gate transition are AETHRION's.
entries.not_owned: Durable execution, retries, timers and replay determinism.
entries.authority_boundary: Temporal is the process authority — it decides when a transition may be attempted, never whether the evidence supports it. A workflow may not compute a gate verdict; it calls the Gate Service and records what came back.
entries.not_used: Temporal's own visibility store as a scientific record, and any non-deterministic work inside workflow code.

entries.name: NATS JetStream
entries.owned_contract: The event envelope, subject taxonomy and the transactional outbox that decides what is published at all.
entries.not_owned: Stream storage, delivery guarantees, consumer groups and replay mechanics.
entries.authority_boundary: The event plane carries events and never authority. An event is a notification that something was decided elsewhere; nothing becomes true because a message arrived, and no consumer may treat an event as a gate input.
entries.not_used: NATS as a canonical store, and any control flow that depends on delivery order.

entries.name: LangGraph
entries.owned_contract: The bounded-cognition runtime contract: what a task may reason over, for how long, and with which context projection.
entries.not_owned: Graph execution, state channels and checkpointing.
entries.authority_boundary: Cognition is bounded inside one task and never spans a gate. A LangGraph run may produce a hypothesis, a draft or a recommendation; it may not carry state across a gate boundary and it holds no verdict authority.
entries.not_used: LangGraph persistence as the canonical record of a reasoning step.

entries.name: LiteLLM
entries.owned_contract: The `ModelGateway` contract: admission, routing policy, data-class redaction, cost attribution and the fail-closed decision.
entries.not_owned: Provider SDK abstraction, streaming transport and provider-specific error translation.
entries.authority_boundary: The gateway routes and accounts; it never decides whether a model may be used for a task. Admission is WP-044's decision, recorded as a capability profile, and a gateway fallback may not silently substitute a model that was never admitted.
entries.not_used: LiteLLM's own key store as the credential authority, and its cache as a source of results that are treated as fresh.

entries.name: Inspect AI
entries.owned_contract: The behaviours themselves, their pass criteria, the golden sets and the contamination controls — encoded as Inspect tasks, solvers and scorers.
entries.not_owned: The evaluation engine: dataset/solver/scorer execution, sandboxing, limits, retry/resume and transcripts.
entries.authority_boundary: A scorer result is a `VerificationResult`, never a `GateRecord` verdict. Inspect measures; gate policy decides. An Inspect transcript is operational evidence and is not the canonical run record.
entries.not_used: Inspect as the canonical evidence store, and its scores as claim confidence.
entries.source: docs/architecture/AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §4 — 'WP-043 changes character: from build an evaluation engine to encode AIRL behaviours as Inspect tasks and scorers'

entries.name: GROBID
entries.owned_contract: `SourceRepresentation` — which parser, which version, which digest produced the representation a span is anchored to.
entries.not_owned: Scholarly PDF → TEI XML extraction.
entries.authority_boundary: A parser produces a representation, never an interpretation. A re-parse creates `representation-v2` and does not invalidate a claim anchored to v1; the claim stays bound to the representation that actually supported it.
entries.not_used: GROBID's own confidence scores as evidence quality, and its output as canonical text without a recorded digest.

entries.name: Pub2TEI
entries.owned_contract: The requirement that a span means the same thing regardless of where the source came from.
entries.not_owned: Normalisation of Elsevier, Springer, Wiley and JATS/NLM XML into TEI.
entries.authority_boundary: Normalisation may change representation and never meaning. A publisher-supplied structure that disagrees with the PDF is a recorded discrepancy, not a silent preference.
entries.not_used: Publisher metadata as authority over the source registry.

entries.name: PaperQA2
entries.owned_contract: How retrieval binds to provenance and claim scope — the retrieval contract, not the retriever.
entries.not_owned: Iterative retrieval, ranking and answer synthesis at runtime.
entries.authority_boundary: Retrieval supplies candidates and never a claim. Nothing retrieved becomes evidence until it is anchored as an `EvidenceSpan` against a stored representation.
entries.not_used: PaperQA2's answers as claim text, and its citations as verified references.
entries.notes: Two decisions exist about this upstream and they do not conflict: the runtime retrieval service is adopted behind an adapter (this entry), while three of its algorithmic mechanisms are reimplemented natively (`ASM-017`, ADAPTIVE_REIMPLEMENT). An implementer needs both rows.

entries.name: OpenScholar
entries.owned_contract: The same adapter contract as PaperQA2, deliberately — so the two remain comparable.
entries.not_owned: Retrieval and self-feedback sufficiency at runtime.
entries.authority_boundary: Retrieval supplies candidates and never a claim, exactly as for PaperQA2.
entries.not_used: Any hard-coded preference between the two retrievers before the bake-off runs.
entries.selection: Not chosen. The choice is settled by measurement on the same questions, corpus and budget against source recall, citation correctness, entailment, coverage, unsupported-claim rate, latency and cost — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §5.

entries.name: ASReview
entries.owned_contract: The screening decision record, the stopping rule and the coverage claim that follows from it.
entries.not_owned: Active-learning ranking of candidate records.
entries.authority_boundary: Screening ranks; it never excludes. An exclusion is a recorded human or policy decision with a reason, and a stopping rule reports coverage rather than declaring completeness.
entries.not_used: Model-suggested exclusion as an exclusion.

entries.name: Cedar
entries.owned_contract: The `PolicyDecision` interface — what WP-056 delivers. The engine behind it is configuration.
entries.not_owned: Policy evaluation, schema validation and bundle semantics.
entries.authority_boundary: The interface is the contract, not the backend. A policy engine answers a question the architecture asked; it may not extend the question, and default deny is a property of the interface rather than of the engine.
entries.not_used: Cedar's schema as the canonical contract model.
entries.selection: Not chosen — ADR-010. Cedar and OPA are both optional backends behind one interface, and the bake-off that decides between them cannot run until a policy set exists.

entries.name: OPA / Rego
entries.owned_contract: The `PolicyDecision` interface, as for Cedar.
entries.not_owned: Policy evaluation and bundle distribution.
entries.authority_boundary: As for Cedar: the interface is the contract, not the backend.
entries.not_used: Rego as the language in which AETHRION's authority model is expressed.
entries.selection: Not chosen — ADR-010. Note that WP-056 was once titled *OPA Policy Platform*; that title was a preference wearing a decision's clothes and the package now names the decision point rather than an engine.

entries.name: gVisor
entries.owned_contract: The `ExecutionBackend` interface and the risk-profile → backend routing.
entries.not_owned: Syscall interception and kernel-level isolation.
entries.authority_boundary: Isolation technology enforces a boundary the policy decided; it never decides the boundary. A sandbox escape is a control failure, not a permission grant.
entries.not_used: The sandbox as the only control — ADR-003 puts the boundary at the capability, not at the isolation layer.
entries.selection: Routing by risk profile, not a single choice: gVisor, E2B and the Inspect sandbox are alternative backends behind one interface — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §6.

entries.name: E2B
entries.owned_contract: The `ExecutionBackend` interface, as for gVisor.
entries.not_owned: Hosted sandbox provisioning and lifecycle.
entries.authority_boundary: As for gVisor. A hosted backend additionally may not become an egress path that the default-deny proxy has not seen — WP-057.
entries.not_used: E2B as a data-plane store for anything the evidence path needs.
entries.selection: Alternative backend behind the same interface; routing is by risk profile — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §6.

entries.name: S3 Object Lock semantics
entries.owned_contract: The `ImmutableObjectStore` contract, and the proof that delete and overwrite are actually refused.
entries.not_owned: Compliance-mode WORM retention enforcement.
entries.authority_boundary: The store refuses mutation; it does not decide what deserves to be immutable. Retention class is a policy decision recorded before the object is written.
entries.not_used: Governance mode, and any bucket configuration in which an administrator can shorten retention.
entries.selection: Qualified implementation not yet named. AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW and other S3-compatible implementations differ in whether compliance mode is genuinely enforced; the bake-off criterion is a demonstrated refusal of delete and overwrite by a root-equivalent identity within the retention window.
entries.source: docs/architecture/AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §7 — 'WP-026 changes character: from build a content-addressed WORM store to integrate and verify an existing object-lock implementation'

entries.name: lakeFS
entries.owned_contract: The separation itself — working datasets are not accepted evidence.
entries.not_owned: Git-like branching over object storage.
entries.authority_boundary: A working dataset branch is never an evidence reference. Nothing on a mutable branch may be cited by a claim; promotion into the immutable store is an explicit, recorded act.
entries.not_used: lakeFS as the store for accepted evidence.
entries.selection: Optional and separable from the WORM decision — a different problem, deliberately kept separate.

entries.name: MLflow
entries.owned_contract: The Run Registry, the preflight validator and the binding from a run to a `RawEvaluatorArtifact` and a `VerifiedValue`.
entries.not_owned: Experiment tracking, parameter/metric storage and the tracking UI.
entries.authority_boundary: MLflow answers *what did the system do*. It never answers *what may be believed* — that is a signed `EvidenceManifest` plus Workflow Run RO-Crate. Operational telemetry is not provenance, and an MLflow metric is not a `VerifiedValue`.
entries.not_used: MLflow as the scientific truth store, and its model registry as the admission authority.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry
entries.owned_contract: The end-to-end correlation identifier standard — WP-011 — and which spans must exist for a run to be reconstructable.
entries.not_owned: Trace/metric/log collection and OTLP transport.
entries.authority_boundary: Telemetry is operational and never evidential. A missing span is an observability defect; it is not proof that a step did not happen, and a present span is not proof that it did.
entries.not_used: Traces as the audit ledger — that is WP-099.

entries.name: sigstore-python
entries.owned_contract: The attestation profile and what a signature is taken to mean. The named upgrade out of `airl-interim-v0.1`.
entries.not_owned: Keyless OIDC identity, certificate issuance and the Rekor inclusion proof.
entries.authority_boundary: A signature establishes who issued an artifact and that it has not changed. It never establishes that the content is correct, and a verified signature is not an acceptance.
entries.not_used: Sigstore identity as an AETHRION role binding.
entries.notes: Renaming the interim profile `airl-interim-v0.1` or the `https://airl-os.local/…` predicateType invalidates a signature that verifies today — AGENTS.md §7.5.

entries.name: OpenSSF model-signing
entries.owned_contract: The requirement that a local open-weight model file has a verified identity before it is admitted.
entries.not_owned: Signing and verification of model files.
entries.authority_boundary: A signed model file is an admitted *artifact*, not a qualified *actor*. Qualification is WP-044's measurement.
entries.not_used: A vendor signature as evidence of capability.

entries.name: OpenTimestamps
entries.owned_contract: What is anchored, and the statement that today's profile is tamper-evident but not externally witnessed.
entries.not_owned: The timestamp proof and its verification path.
entries.authority_boundary: An anchor establishes that something existed by a time. It says nothing about who produced it or whether it is true.
entries.not_used: The anchor as a substitute for an independent verifier.

entries.name: Workflow Run RO-Crate
entries.owned_contract: Which run facts must be present for a run to be re-executable by someone who was not there.
entries.not_owned: The crate format and its PROV mapping.
entries.authority_boundary: A crate records what ran. It does not assert that the result supports a claim; that binding is the `EvidenceManifest`'s.
entries.not_used: Any AETHRION-specific run format that would fork the standard.
entries.conformance: Not yet written. Priority raised in AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §7: adopt before the first slice, so the run format is never forked.

entries.name: Croissant 1.1
entries.owned_contract: The dataset record and the policy input a usage condition becomes.
entries.not_owned: The dataset description format, its PROV-O provenance and its ODRL/DUO usage conditions.
entries.authority_boundary: A declared usage condition is a policy *input*, never a policy decision. The PDP decides whether a use is permitted.
entries.not_used: Croissant metadata as evidence of dataset quality.

entries.name: SWHID
entries.owned_contract: Where a software identity is required in the evidence chain.
entries.not_owned: The identifier scheme itself.
entries.authority_boundary: An intrinsic identifier establishes identity, not availability and not correctness. Computing one does not archive the code.
entries.not_used: SWHID as a substitute for an environment manifest.

entries.name: SEPIO
entries.owned_contract: The AIRL profile over SEPIO's core — which relation types are used and what each licenses.
entries.not_owned: The assertion/evidence/provenance core model.
entries.authority_boundary: A model of assertions is not an assertion about truth. SEPIO gives the shape; the gate decides what may be believed.
entries.not_used: SEPIO's full ontology where the profile does not use it.
entries.conformance: Not yet written. Generated from one LinkML model — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §9.

entries.name: LinkML
entries.owned_contract: The single contract model from which JSON Schema, Pydantic, JSON-LD, SHACL and SQL DDL are generated.
entries.not_owned: Code and schema generation.
entries.authority_boundary: A generator produces representations of a model; it never decides the model. A generated artifact that disagrees with the model is a defect in the model or the generator, never a third opinion.
entries.not_used: Hand-written parallel definitions of a contract that the model already generates.
entries.notes: This attacks a real debt: contracts currently risk being defined three times in three shapes, which is how the bridge and the contract core came to disagree about digests — finding H4.

entries.name: Pandoc
entries.owned_contract: Every AIRL transformation, expressed as an AST filter.
entries.not_owned: The document AST, citeproc, reference templates and Lua filter execution.
entries.authority_boundary: A renderer formats what the compiler decided; it never changes what a document asserts. **AIRL transformations are AST filters, never regexes over a manuscript.**
entries.not_used: Any transformation that edits rendered output after the fact.

entries.name: Quarto
entries.owned_contract: The publication package contract and what a rendered artifact must contain.
entries.not_owned: Manuscript orchestration, cross references, multi-format render, JATS output and MECA bundling.
entries.authority_boundary: As for Pandoc: rendering never changes an assertion.
entries.not_used: Quarto's computation cache as a source of results.
entries.selection: **Provisional** until the bake-off against MyST runs. None of this toolchain is installed here, so 'this project uses Quarto' states an intention, not a measurement — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §9.1.

entries.name: MyST
entries.owned_contract: The publication package contract, as for Quarto.
entries.not_owned: The authoring and render stack.
entries.authority_boundary: As for Quarto.
entries.not_used: Any stack-specific syntax in canonical content.
entries.selection: The competing stack in the bake-off — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §9.1.

entries.name: CSL
entries.owned_contract: Which style a venue requires; nothing more.
entries.not_owned: Citation style definitions and their rendering.
entries.authority_boundary: A citation style is presentation. It never changes which source supports a claim.
entries.not_used: An AIRL-invented citation style — AETHRION does not invent one.
entries.conformance: Style conformance is checked against the venue's declared requirement.

entries.name: veraPDF
entries.owned_contract: The accessibility contract the rendered artifact must satisfy.
entries.not_owned: PDF/A and PDF/UA validation.
entries.authority_boundary: A validator reports conformance to a format profile. It does not assess whether the document is readable by a person, and a pass is not an accessibility claim.
entries.not_used: A validator pass as evidence that WCAG 2.2 is met.
entries.conformance: WCAG 2.2 contracts validated against the rendered artifact — AETHRION_COMPONENT_REUSE.md §9.1.

entries.name: statcheck · grim · pysprite
entries.owned_contract: Which forensic test runs at which gate, and what a failure means for the claim.
entries.not_owned: The statistical consistency tests themselves.
entries.authority_boundary: A forensic finding is a `VerificationResult` that opens an investigation. It is never a finding of misconduct and never a gate verdict — `investigating-integrity-concerns` governs what happens next.
entries.not_used: A test failure as an accusation, or a test pass as evidence of integrity.
entries.notes: Validated implementations are used because the edge cases — scale granularity, rounding, integer constraints — are exactly where a fresh implementation goes wrong.

entries.name: krippendorff · statsmodels · scikit-learn
entries.owned_contract: Which estimator answers which question, and the decision rule written before the data is seen.
entries.not_owned: The estimators.
entries.authority_boundary: An agreement coefficient measures agreement, not correctness. Two reviewers who agree may both be wrong, and a high coefficient is never evidence that a verdict is right.
entries.not_used: An estimator chosen after seeing the result — `preregistration-discipline` forbids it.

entries.name: CaMeL
entries.owned_contract: The trusted-control / untrusted-data architecture and the capability gate that enforces it.
entries.not_owned: Nothing is called at runtime — the idea is implemented here.
entries.authority_boundary: Control flow comes from trusted intent. Untrusted content may supply values; it can never create actions or expand permissions. Content crosses the boundary, authority does not.
entries.not_used: Prompt-layer injection detection as a security boundary — a detector is defence in depth, not a boundary.
entries.notes: WP-136 changes character: from *prompt-injection detection* to **trusted control / untrusted data architecture**.

entries.name: Manubot
entries.owned_contract: Manuscript-as-code discipline: continuous rebuild and citation by identifier.
entries.not_owned: Nothing is called at runtime.
entries.authority_boundary: A build discipline says nothing about what the manuscript may claim.
entries.not_used: Manubot as a second render engine — taken as discipline, not as an engine.

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.owned_contract: The canonical record model and which registry is the authority for which field — WP-012's field-level authority matrix.
entries.not_owned: Relational storage, HA, replication and backup mechanics.
entries.authority_boundary: The database stores canonical records; it never decides what is canonical. Two stores holding the same field is a defect in the ownership matrix, not a reconciliation problem to solve at query time.
entries.not_used: Application logic in the database, and any derived read model treated as a source of truth.

entries.name: Neo4j · pgvector · OpenSearch
entries.owned_contract: The projection contracts and the rebuild that proves a derived model can be destroyed and reconstructed from the canonical store.
entries.not_owned: Graph, vector and full-text query execution.
entries.authority_boundary: A derived read model is never a source of truth. Anything that exists only in a projection is lost by definition, and a projection that disagrees with the canonical store is rebuilt rather than corrected.
entries.not_used: A projection as the only copy of anything the evidence path needs.

entries.name: Kubernetes
entries.owned_contract: The trust-zone segmentation and the `ExecutionProfile` that decides where a workload may run.
entries.not_owned: Scheduling, node lifecycle and workload orchestration.
entries.authority_boundary: The scheduler places work that policy already permitted. Placement is never a permission, and a namespace boundary is not the trust boundary — ADR-003 puts that at the capability.
entries.not_used: Cluster RBAC as the AETHRION role model.

entries.name: Kueue
entries.owned_contract: The quota and priority policy, and the rule that budget pressure degrades verbosity rather than assurance.
entries.not_owned: Queueing, quota enforcement and preemption.
entries.authority_boundary: A queue decides when work runs, never whether it may. A task that cannot afford its required assurance is `BLOCKED`, not run more cheaply — ADR-011.
entries.not_used: Priority as a route around a non-waivable control.

entries.name: SPIFFE / SPIRE and Vault
entries.owned_contract: Which identity may hold which capability, and the scoped, short-lived credential injected only after a `PolicyDecision`.
entries.not_owned: Workload attestation, SVID issuance and secret storage.
entries.authority_boundary: An identity system proves who is asking. It never decides what the asker may do — that is the policy decision point, and a valid identity with no grant is a denial.
entries.not_used: A long-lived credential held by an agent, and any secret reachable from the untrusted data plane.

entries.name: Langfuse
entries.owned_contract: Prompt governance: which prompt version ran, under which policy, against which model fingerprint.
entries.not_owned: Model and agent tracing storage and its UI.
entries.authority_boundary: A trace records what a model was asked and what it said. It is operational evidence and never a scientific record; a prompt that produced a good answer is not thereby a qualified prompt.
entries.not_used: Langfuse scores as evaluation results — those are WP-043's, through Inspect.

entries.name: Grafana
entries.owned_contract: Which six operational graphs must exist, and what each is evidence of.
entries.not_owned: Dashboards, alerting UI and datasource plumbing.
entries.authority_boundary: A dashboard displays; it decides nothing. A green dashboard is not an acceptance, and an alert that nobody can act on is not a control.
entries.not_used: Grafana as an audit ledger — that is WP-099, and it is WORM.

entries.name: Zotero
entries.owned_contract: The canonical source registry and the reconciliation rules. An external edit in Zotero does not automatically become truth here.
entries.not_owned: Reference management, collections, tags and annotation storage.
entries.authority_boundary: Zotero is a working library, never the canonical registry. A record's identity, status and licence position are decided by the source registry service; Zotero is one input to it and one projection of it.
entries.not_used: Zotero item keys as canonical identity, and its collection tree as an authority over inclusion.
entries.version_policy: Pinned through the local Zotero HTTP API surface used by `src/airl_bridge`; the read path is exercised by the test suite on every run.
entries.failure_semantics: Unavailability halts ingest and leaves the last reconciled state intact. The bridge is read-only against Zotero today; nothing is written back.
entries.notes: This is the one component that actually runs. Two open findings against it are recorded in docs/FINDINGS.md history: ingest was capped at 100 records (H1) and there was no deletion reconciliation (H2).

entries.name: Obsidian
entries.owned_contract: The projection contract, the human/generated zone split and the controlled tag vocabulary.
entries.not_owned: Note editing, linking and the local vault format.
entries.authority_boundary: The vault is a projection and never a source. An edit made by hand inside a generated zone is lost on the next mirror, which is the intended behaviour and not a data-loss defect.
entries.not_used: Vault content as canonical knowledge, and any tag invented in a note rather than added to the vocabulary.
entries.version_policy: No plugin dependency; the projection writes plain Markdown with YAML frontmatter, so the format survives an Obsidian upgrade.
entries.failure_semantics: `mirror_plan.py` writes differentially and refuses a target holding files it does not generate — a guard added after it once replaced a vault root.
